Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the present writ petition has been filed to pay the adequate compensation to the petitioner for her commercial land.
He further prays that copy of award has not been provided to her.

3. Learned counsel for the State as well as the National Highways Authority of India submit that the petitioner herself annexed Annexure-3 to the writ petition by which it is clear that a notice to the petitioner under Section 3G of the National Patna High Court CWJC No.12194 of 2022 dt.12-09-2023 Highways Act, 1956 has been issued in Case No. 22 (xvi)/2014- 15 and compensation amount has been calculated to the tune of Rs. 21,88,339/-.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that though the petitioner has received the said Shahin Bano @ Shahina Bano vs The State Of Bihar on 12 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196962912/
1 amount, but the amount of the award should be increased, as proper amount has not been paid for her land.
5.

entities.text: Shahin Bano @ Shahina Bano vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In response thereof, counsel for the National Highways Authority of India submits that since the award has been prepared and amount has been received by the petitioner then in that case, the petitioner has only remedy for enhancement of compensation amount before the Arbitrator under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner has fairly submits that until and unless the award shall not be provided to the petitioner, the petitioner shall not be in a position to calculate the amount accurately for which she is legally entitled for.

7. In this background, the District Land Acquisition Officer, Patna is directed to provide a copy of the award to the petitioner within four weeks from the date of production of a copy of this order by the petitioner before him and upon receiving the award, the petitioner shall be at liberty to raise her Patna High Court CWJC No.12194 of 2022 dt.12-09-2023 grievances under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 before the Arbitrator within six weeks thereafter.
8. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the writ petition stands disposed of.

(Dr. Anshuman, J) Ashwini/-
